transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! That's a good question.

You should avoid any exercise for the first week after your surgery. After that week is up, you can go back to light exercise like gardening. So you'd be able to do some gentle gardening from about a week onwards.

However, you should avoid strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month after surgery.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I was also wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. It's safe to continue using any eye drops or gels you were using before your operation for dry eyes. So you can go ahead and use your eye gel again.

If you're running out and need more, your GP should be able to provide some for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses, especially if it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, or if you have severe light sensitivity along with redness and pain in your eye, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further.

For mild sensitivity, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside, which should help.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses, especially if it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't have your specific details about how long it's been since your operation. If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text:
I had my surgery about a week ago. I guess I expected my vision to be clearer by now. 

But thanks for the information; that makes me feel a bit more at ease. I don't have any more questions right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's good to hear. A week is still very early, so some blurriness is quite normal at this stage and should improve over the coming days and weeks.

Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all of my questions. Thank you so much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and wishing you a smooth recovery.
